## What I did (restructuring only — no feature implemented)

The upcoming change adds `getTelephoneDisplay` on `Owner`, which must split a stored E.164 number into its country code and national digits (e.g. `+61412345678` → `+61` + `412345678`) before grouping them. That country-code knowledge **already existed** — but only as *private* logic buried in `OwnerRestControllerV1`:

- a private `NATIONAL_NUMBER_LENGTHS` map (`"61"→9`, `"1"→10`), and
- `validateNationalNumberLength`, which inline-derived "longest matching country code wins."

Implemented directly, `getTelephoneDisplay` would have had to re-derive that same country-code splitting from scratch — the excess complexity flagged in the task.

This codebase already has a clear idiom for reusable owner-data primitives: documented `public static` methods on `Owner`, each described as "the single definition of X", with consumers delegating (`regionForCity`, `regionForPostcode`, `postcodeRangeForRegion`, `identityKey` — and `validatePostcode` already calls `Owner.postcodeRangeForRegion(Owner.regionForCity(city))`). I moved the telephone country-code knowledge into that same shape:

**`Owner.java`** — added, alongside the existing lookup-table primitives:
- `private static final COUNTRY_CODE_NATIONAL_LENGTHS` (the relocated table)
- `public static String countryCodeOf(String telephone)` — the longest recognized country code an E.164 number carries (the split point the display feature needs)
- `public static Integer nationalNumberLength(String countryCode)` — the per-country national length (mirrors the `regionForPostcode`/`postcodeRangeForRegion` resolver pair)

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — `validateNationalNumberLength` now delegates to `Owner.countryCodeOf` / `Owner.nationalNumberLength` instead of owning a private table; behavior is provably identical across all cases (`+61`, `+1`, unrecognized).

Both new methods are already in use (by the controller), so there's no dead code. When the change lands, `getTelephoneDisplay` can simply call `countryCodeOf(this.telephone)` to obtain the country code and national digits, and only the human-grouping/formatting — the genuinely new part — needs writing.
